transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-02-25
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 9 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Narayan (Redwood SA), Anna Müller (MedData Head of Security), Liam O'Connor (IT Ops), Sofia Rossi (Legal), Jakub Nowak (Platform), Elena Petrova (Data Privacy)

Summary (auto): Discussed region pinning, EU residency, sub-processors, encryption/KMS, retention of audit logs, and next steps for technical deep dive.

00:00 Samantha Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we really appreciate you taking the time. Quick intro we're Redwood Inference, Samantha AE, Carlos is our SE, Priya who does infra arch.
00:12 Anna Müller: Hi, Anna here, Head of Security at MedData, we've got legal and platform on the line too.
00:18 Liam O'Connor: Liam - ops.
00:21 Carlos Rivera: Thanks Anna. The goals for today as I understand: deep dive on data residency, region pinning, and KMS/integration, right?
00:29 Anna Müller: Correct. We process EU patient records; anything processed or stored in the US is complicated for us. We need to know where tokens, logs, and intermediate artifacts live.
00:38 Priya Narayan: Absolutely. We'll walk through our Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options — and how pinning and routing works. Also cover audit logs and sub-processor list.
00:47 Sofia Rossi: From legal: we need clarity on cross-border processing and a list of sub-processors with locations. Also what data Redwood may access for ops or troubleshooting.
00:58 Carlos Rivera: Right, good callout. High level: in Hosted, requests by default route to the nearest region, but we support region pinning policy — you can lock a customer to a region (e.g., eu-west-1) so inference and logs remain in that region. For stronger controls we offer Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in region) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) which gives you maximum isolation.
01:18 Jakub Nowak: When you say logs remain, do you mean audit logs, raw request bodies, or derivative telemetry? We need guarantees about PII not leaving EU.
01:26 Carlos Rivera: Yeah, good question. By default we collect telemetry for reliability but for EU-pinned customers we can opt to disable storing request payloads in our central telemetry. Audit logs — like auth events, usage — can be retained and stored in the pinned region. There are some caveats around managed backups and support access that we'll detail in the sub-processor and data flow docs.
01:45 Anna Müller: And encryption? We have corporate KMS and would prefer to bring our own key. Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
01:52 Priya Narayan: Yes. For Dedicated and Private we support KMS integration and customer-managed keys. In Hosted we offer KMS integration via BYOK for certain enterprise tiers — the key material is in your KMS and we use envelope encryption. For on-prem we can also integrate with HSMs but that's part of the Private engagement.
02:08 Elena Petrova: Quick — is the model weights considered personal data if we fine-tune on customer data? We want to avoid sending patient data outside EU in fine-tunes.
02:17 Carlos Rivera: We recommend separate processes — for any fine-tuning you can run in your Private deployment or in an EU dedicated pool; Redwood will not use your training data for model improvement unless you opt in.
02:27 Sofia Rossi: Can you confirm that statement in writing? Non-opt-in data will not be used for model training.
02:31 Samantha Lee: We'll share the policy statement and SOC artifacts.
02:34 Carlos Rivera: Also, region pinning works at project/account level — you can set default region in the console and enforce via org policy. For cross-border routing we have explicit flags: no-cross-border which will fail requests if the pinned region is unavailable. The fallback behavior is configurable — either fail closed or route to an approved secondary region.
02:54 Liam O'Connor: If we set fail-closed, what's the SLA implication? We need to understand expected downtime if region is down.
03:02 Priya Narayan: If fail-closed is enabled and the region is unavailable, requests will be rejected. For high availability we recommend multi-region pinned pair (primary EU + secondary EU) or Dedicated with multi-AZ within the region. We'll include HA topology options in the doc.
03:18 Anna Müller: Sub-processors — who else touches data? We need to list AWS accounts, monitoring providers, and any translation service.
03:26 Carlos Rivera: Our sub-processor list includes cloud infra providers (AWS, GCP in some regions), monitoring (Datadog or internal), and SSO providers for auth. For Hosted EU customers, the infra is in EU region accounts. We'll share the full sub-processor list and location mapping.
03:40 Jakub Nowak: You mentioned backups earlier — where do backups land? Are snapshots replicated to US by default?
03:47 Carlos Rivera: For EU-pinned accounts, backups are stored in-region. There are options where cross-region backups are enabled for disaster recovery — but those are opt-in and documented. By default, backups respect region pinning.
03:58 Anna Müller: Okay that's good. What about logs used for debugging — are engineers ever allowed to access raw request content?
04:05 Carlos Rivera: Access is strictly role-based. Support engineers can only access minimal logs and must go through an audit workflow. For EU-residency customers we can disable raw payload logging for Hosted and grant access only under scoped procedures. We also provide signed audit logs on request.
04:20 Sofia Rossi: We need to know retention windows for audit logs and how to export them.
04:25 Priya Narayan: Audit logs retention is configurable. Default is 90 days in Hosted, but enterprise plans allow custom retention, and you can export logs to your S3 bucket in-region. We'll include the export configuration.
04:38 Anna Müller: About encryption at rest — do you use customer keys for DBs and object storage?
04:43 Carlos Rivera: For Dedicated/Private yes. In Hosted, by default we manage keys, but bring-your-own-key is supported for enterprise tiers. We'll note where envelope keys are used.
04:52 Liam O'Connor: Cross-border processing — what about sub-processors that have US-based staff who might access EU data? Any binding clauses or SCCs?
04:59 Samantha Lee: We use standard EU SCCs and DPAs. We'll share our DPA and sub-processor agreements. For staff access, roles are limited and covered under contractual terms.
05:10 Jakub Nowak: Is there logging of administrative access and commands run by Redwood engineers? We need immutable audit trails.
05:16 Priya Narayan: Yes, there is privileged access logging. We produce tamper-evident audit records and can provide time-stamped exports.
05:24 Elena Petrova: A quick point — can we use region pinning but still have low latency for EU users? If you pin to eu-west-1, what's typical median latency to your models?
05:34 Carlos Rivera: Latency depends on model size and infra. For smaller models 50-120ms, larger ones 200-400ms median depending on prompt. We'll share performance profiles per model and region; there's also edge routing for proxied requests to reduce egress times.
05:50 Anna Müller: We also have strict requirements for legal: vendor can not subcontract certain PII processing to non-EU sub-processors. Is that feasible?
05:58 Carlos Rivera: We can work with contractual restrictions; some customers require Dedicated or Private to meet that. For Hosted we can provide in-region infra but some third-party services may be outside EU — we'll make an exceptions list.
06:10 Sofia Rossi: Can you outline the difference practically between Dedicated and Private for us? We want clear tradeoffs (cost, control, compliance).
06:18 Priya Narayan: Sure: Dedicated = reserved capacity in customer-only pools, isolated compute, but infra still runs in Redwood-managed cloud accounts; good for strong isolation and lower ops burden. Private = customer-managed control plane or on-prem deployment, full VPC, no Redwood-managed compute in shared accounts, maximum control and suitable for highest compliance. We'll send a side-by-side matrix.
06:36 Anna Müller: Great. A few specific asks: a) signed statement that public Hosted won't process EU patient data in US if region pinned; b) list of sub-processors with country mapping; c) sample DPA and SCCs; d) KMS integration steps.
06:50 Samantha Lee: We'll provide those. Carlos will take the region/sub-processor technical items; Priya will handle VPC details; I'll send legal artifacts.
06:58 Jakub Nowak: Can we see an example policy JSON for pinning and fail-closed? We want to automate enforcement.
07:04 Carlos Rivera: Yep, will include sample policy and API call examples plus console screenshots.
07:12 Anna Müller: Also please include the escalation procedure for when support needs to access data — we need RBAC and approval workflow documented.
07:18 Priya Narayan: We'll include the approval flow, audit evidence, and optional e-discovery controls.
07:25 Sofia Rossi: On the contract side, we may need to add narrow clauses about subcontractor locations. We'll review DPA when you send it.
07:31 Samantha Lee: Understood. Any other technical blockers?
07:36 Liam O'Connor: One more — can you ingest logs into our SIEM? We have Splunk in-region.
07:42 Carlos Rivera: Yes, you can forward logs to your S3 or directly to Splunk via secure collector in region.
07:48 Elena Petrova: For PII redaction — do you offer any automatic redaction before sending to Redwood?
07:53 Carlos Rivera: We have client-side SDK hooks and can redact at the edge. For Hosted, we recommend preprocessing to strip PHI, or using hosted transformations in your VPC pipeline.
08:05 Anna Müller: Thank you. Let's recap next steps.
08:09 Samantha Lee: Recap: we'll share SOC2/ISO, DPA, sub-processor list, region pinning docs, policy samples, KMS integration guide, and schedule VPC deep dive. Action items and dates will be in the follow-up email.
08:20 Sofia Rossi: Perfect, we'll review and follow up with legal questions.
08:24 Samantha Lee: Great — thanks everyone, we'll send the artifacts and calendar invite for the tech deep dive.
08:30 (call ends)

Notes: Transcription flagged a few words; some names may be mis-typed (Jakub/Jacob). Links shared during call: https://redwood.ai/security (placeholder), https://redwood.ai/subprocessors (placeholder), deck: tinyurl.com/redwood-regionpin (placeholder).

End of transcript.
